events.title: Buford on the ridge
events.text: Buford's cavalry division reached Gettysburg at eleven yesterday morning, just as a detachment of Heth's Confederate division was about to enter. The detachment withdrew toward Cashtown, and Buford deployed along the ridge east of Willoughby Run, between the Mummasburg and Fairfield Roads, with pickets pushed well forward. At five this morning Heth's division leaves Cashtown on the Chambersburg Pike, Archer's and Davis's brigades leading.

events.title: McPherson's Ridge
events.text: Buford's vedettes fired on Heth's advance at Marsh Creek, four miles from Gettysburg, about half past seven. Between eight and nine Archer and Davis deploy on Herr Ridge, supported by Pegram's artillery. Gamble's brigade, dismounted, with Calef's battery on both sides of the Pike, holds them for more than two hours.

events.title: Reynolds and the Iron Brigade
events.text: Cutler's brigade arrived at 9:45 on the right of Reynolds's Woods, three regiments north of the railroad cut: Wadsworth's division is the first Union infantry on the field. At ten the Iron Brigade charges Archer's brigade in Reynolds's Woods, drives it back over Willoughby Run and captures Archer. Reynolds is killed at the edge of the woods about ten o'clock. Wainwright's batteries come up between ten and eleven.

events.title: The railroad cut
events.text: Davis's brigade formed west of Herr's Tavern at ten and crossed the run north of the Pike. It drives back Hall's 2nd Maine Battery and Cutler's right, then wheels into the railroad cut, which is too deep and steep to defend. Around eleven the 6th Wisconsin and the 84th and 95th New York take many prisoners and a stand of colors there.

events.title: The noon lull
events.text: By half past eleven the field is quiet. Rowley's division came up about eleven, Biddle's brigade on the left of Reynolds's Woods facing west and Stone's at the McPherson buildings. Robinson's division reaches the Seminary about noon and builds breastworks there. Rodes's division comes down the Carlisle Road and occupies Oak Hill, and Early's arrives by the Harrisburg Road. The XI Corps marches through the town; Barlow's two brigades arrive about noon, Schurz's about one.

events.title: Iverson's Pits
events.text: 'At 2 P.M., both sides were reinforced and the fighting resumed.' Rodes's guns open from Oak Hill and force Wainwright's forward batteries back. O'Neal's three regiments, then Iverson's four, attack Baxter's line behind the stone wall east of Forney's field. Iverson's brigade is nearly destroyed by fire from front and flank; Baxter and Cutler take 1,000 prisoners and three stands of colors. Daniel's brigade fights Stone's at the railroad cuts, and Pettigrew and Brockenbrough cross Willoughby Run against the Iron Brigade and Biddle.

events.title: Barlow's Knoll
events.text: Lee arrived about half past two. About three Gordon's brigade crosses Rock Creek and charges Barlow's Knoll, and Hays and Hoke advance on the flank of the XI Corps and take two guns; Jones's battalion enfilades von Gilsa from a knoll east of the creek. Doles comes in from the west, and von Gilsa is forced back to the Almshouse. About half past three Coster's brigade marches through the town to Kuhn's brickyard to hold Hays and Hoke off the corps' line of retreat.

events.title: Through the town
events.text: Perrin, Lane and Scales crossed Willoughby Run about half past three. 'At 4 P.M. the Confederates advanced in superior numbers and enveloped both flanks.' Scales's brigade charges the line on Seminary Ridge and loses all but one field officer; Perrin's breaks it and pursues into the town; Lane fights Buford's cavalry at the stone wall south of the Fairfield Road. The I Corps falls back to Cemetery Hill, and the XI Corps goes back through crowded streets; Schimmelfennig is trapped in the town.

events.title: Cemetery Hill
events.text: Hancock arrived after four. Wadsworth's division forms on the north slope of Culp's Hill, Robinson's and Rowley's south of the cemetery facing the Emmitsburg Road, and Buford's cavalry on the left of the town. Hays and Hoke halt on East High Street, and Doles at the town's southern edge. Geary's division comes up the Baltimore Pike about five. Ewell does not attack Cemetery Hill. Almost 9,000 Union and slightly over 6,000 Confederate soldiers have fallen today.

events.title: The first night
events.text: Stannard's Vermont brigade arrived at dusk, and Ward's brigade of Birney's division after sunset. Johnson's division, too late for the fighting, moves through the town in the night to the Hanover Road east of Rock Creek, Steuart's brigade a mile beyond the creek. Anderson's division takes Heth's old position west of Willoughby Run around dark. Hazard's II Corps batteries reach the Taneytown Road three miles from Gettysburg at eleven.

events.title: The fishhook forms
events.text: Humphreys's division came up by a road two miles west at one in the morning. At six Greene's brigade takes position on Culp's Hill. The II Corps arrives on the Taneytown Road between six and eight, and Birney relieves Geary on the left near Little Round Top. The V Corps lies on the Baltimore Pike near Rock Creek.

events.title: Longstreet's march
events.text: Lee gave his orders at eleven. Late in the forenoon Wilcox's 10th and 11th Alabama take the right of Anderson's line on Seminary Ridge after a severe skirmish with Berdan's sharpshooters in Pitzer's Woods. About noon Law's brigade rejoins Hood after a 25-mile march begun at three in the morning. McLaws's division turns right at the Black Horse Tavern, crosses Willoughby Run farther downstream and forms. Gregg's cavalry reaches the Hanover Road, and Buford's two brigades leave for Taneytown.

events.title: Sickles to the Peach Orchard
events.text: Shortly after two Birney's division wheels left onto the high ground from Plum Run to the Peach Orchard and along the Emmitsburg Road to the Sherfy house: Ward on the left, de Trobriand in the centre, Graham at the Peach Orchard. Humphreys's division goes forward to the Emmitsburg Road between two and three, Carr in front and Brewster behind. By half past three the salient stands and Little Round Top is empty.

events.title: Hood attacks
events.text: Barksdale reached Warfield Ridge about three, Kershaw and Semmes at half past, Wofford at four, and Hood's four brigades formed south of them about four. 'At about 4 P.M. the batteries opened fire. Soon after, the division advanced.' Latimer's battalion opens from Benner's Hill. The V Corps leaves the Baltimore Pike for the left.

events.title: Devil's Den and Little Round Top
events.text: Robertson's 1st Texas and 3rd Arkansas and Law's 44th and 48th Alabama go into Devil's Den and the Triangular Field and take three of Smith's guns. The 4th and 5th Texas and the 4th, 15th and 47th Alabama climb against Little Round Top. Vincent's brigade, detached after four, takes the hill ten minutes before them, the 20th Maine on its left. Hood is wounded on Slyder's lane.

events.title: Rose Woods and the Wheatfield
events.text: Kershaw advanced about half past four against the Peach Orchard's south face and the Loop. G. T. Anderson's Georgians go into Rose Woods against de Trobriand's 17th Maine at the Wheatfield wall. Tilton and Sweitzer, at the edge of Rose Woods facing the Rose house, are attacked and draw back across the Wheatfield Road: the first break in Birney's line. Weed's brigade reaches the summit of Little Round Top in time for the 140th New York, with Hazlett's battery.

events.title: Barksdale's charge
events.text: Semmes advanced about five in support of Kershaw and Anderson and is mortally wounded near the Loop. Barksdale's tablet says his brigade advanced at five; Birney's puts it at half past six, and this replay starts it at half past five. Barksdale's four Mississippi regiments go for the Peach Orchard, held by Graham's brigade and McGilvery's guns on the Wheatfield Road.

events.title: Caldwell in the Wheatfield
events.text: Caldwell's division came in between five and six: Cross and Kelly along the stone wall east of the field, Zook on the right, Brooke across a marsh to the crest of a wooded hill. Cross and Zook are killed. Ayres's regulars cross Plum Run to Houck's Ridge. Wofford is ordered forward about six along the Wheatfield Road and, with Semmes and Kershaw, turns Caldwell's flank. Of 20,444 men engaged in the Wheatfield, about 30 percent fall.

events.title: Wilcox, Wright and the 1st Minnesota
events.text: Graham's brigade is broken at the Sherfy house about half past six and Graham is captured; Humphreys's division changes front and falls back across Plum Run, and Sickles is wounded. At six Wilcox broke the line on the Emmitsburg Road and Wright drove the 15th Massachusetts and 82nd New York from near the Codori house; Wright breaks through the wall south of the Angle to the crest of the ridge. The 1st Minnesota's 262 men charge Wilcox, and 215 fall.

events.title: Culp's Hill at dusk
events.text: Jones's and Steuart's brigades crossed Rock Creek at six and climb Culp's Hill, Nicholls's on Jones's left. Most of the XII Corps left the hill at half past six to seven for the left of the line. Greene's 1,400 hold four distinct charges, the 137th New York refusing the right, with about 750 men from the I and XI Corps.

events.title: McCandless clears the valley
events.text: About sunset Wofford drives Ayres's regulars back to Little Round Top, half of them lost, and falls back to the grove west of the Wheatfield. After sunset McCandless's Pennsylvania Reserves, with Nevin's VI Corps brigade, charge from the north slope of Little Round Top across the Plum Run marsh and beyond the stone wall into the Wheatfield. The VI Corps came up after a march of over 30 miles; Russell's and Torbert's brigades go to the extreme left. At seven Willard's brigade charged Barksdale's Mississippians in the Plum Run swale; Willard was killed and Barksdale mortally wounded. Stannard's and Rowley's brigades take 80 prisoners and 4 guns on the Emmitsburg Road.

events.title: East Cemetery Hill
events.text: Hays's and Hoke's brigades charge out of the low ground, plant their colors on the lunettes and break into Wiedrich's and Ricketts's batteries; the cannoneers fight 'with handspikes, rammers, and stones'. Carroll's brigade from Ziegler's Grove and Krzyzanowski's regiments retake the guns, and the attack is repulsed between nine and ten. Avery is mortally wounded. On Culp's Hill Steuart's 3rd North Carolina and 1st Maryland take the works on the lesser summit.

events.title: The council of war
events.text: Silence about half past ten; Meade's council meets at midnight. Williams's and Geary's brigades return to Culp's Hill at midnight to find Johnson in their works, and form a line facing them. Perrin and Thomas hold Long Lane, Ramseur, Doles and Iverson on their left. About 10,000 Union and 6,800 Confederate soldiers have fallen today.

events.title: The guns on Culp's Hill
events.text: Daniel's brigade left the town about half past one and reached Culp's Hill about four, O'Neal's at daybreak, Smith's from the York Pike at daylight. At daylight 26 Union guns on the Baltimore Pike, Power's Hill and McAllister's Hill open for about fifteen minutes, and again at half past five. 'A fierce engagement lasted seven hours.'

events.title: Spangler's Spring
events.text: About ten Walker's and Daniel's brigades strike Greene from the east while Steuart advances against Candy and Kane. Colgrove's 2nd Massachusetts and 27th Indiana charge across the swale at Spangler's Spring and are repulsed by Smith's Virginians behind the stone wall. At half past ten the Confederates withdraw to the base of the hill and across Rock Creek, and by eleven the works are retaken. Johnson's division has lost about 2,000.

events.title: The cannonade
events.text: Pickett reached the field about nine; at half past one his division forms east of Spangler's Woods, its right near a barn, Garnett and Kemper in front and Armistead behind. Pettigrew's division is back in its position of the day before, Lane's and Scales's brigades under Trimble behind its right. Hays has burned the Bliss barn. At one 150 to 170 Confederate guns open from the Peach Orchard north along Seminary Ridge, and about 80 Union guns reply. It is 87 degrees at two.

events.title: Pickett's Charge
events.text: 'At 3 P.M. it advanced to assault across roughly three-quarters of a mile of open ground.' Modern writers put the step-off between two and three; every tablet says three, and the replay keeps it. Pickett's three brigades go forward on the right, Pettigrew's four and Trimble's two on the left. Garnett's and Kemper's lines break at the fences along the Emmitsburg Road, re-form and go on to the wall.

events.title: The Angle
events.text: Armistead's men go over the wall into the Angle. Garnett is killed, Armistead mortally wounded and Kemper wounded. Fry's men reach the wall at the Angle, with 13 color bearers shot; Davis's reach the wall south of the Bryan barn. Brockenbrough's brigade, on the left flank, takes fire from front and flank north of the Bryan barn and falls back first. Stannard's 13th and 16th Vermont change front and strike Pickett's right. Hancock and Gibbon are wounded. The charge costs 6,555 Confederates, 2,655 of them Pickett's; Hays's division takes about 1,500 prisoners and 15 stands of colors.

events.title: Farnsworth's charge
events.text: Off the map to the east, Gregg's cavalry turned back Stuart's on the Hanover Road this afternoon; Custer's brigade lost 257. Merritt's brigade marched up the Emmitsburg Road at noon and has fought along it for four hours. At half past five Farnsworth's 18th Pennsylvania, 1st Vermont and 1st West Virginia charge through woods and past stone fences into the Plum Run valley south of Devil's Den; Law's and Robertson's men repulse them, and Farnsworth is killed. About five McCandless swept the Wheatfield and took 200 prisoners and the 15th Georgia's colors. Heavy rain ends Merritt's fight.

events.title: Back to Seminary Ridge
events.text: Johnson's division held the foot of Culp's Hill until ten and pulls back to the ridge north-west of the town; Rodes's brigades go back in the night, and Hays and Hoke follow at two in the morning. Thomas's brigade retires to the ridge after dark, and Benning's to the Emmitsburg Road.

events.title: The rain
events.text: Lee's army stands in line on Seminary Ridge all day in heavy rain. Slocum's reconnaissance with Colgrove's and McDougall's regiments finds no enemy, Schurz's detachment enters the town and takes over 300 Confederates, and Day's regulars force in the pickets on the Confederate right. At two this afternoon Iverson's brigade marches as wagon guard on the road to Hagerstown, and the rest of the army follows in the night.

outcome.result: Lee's attacks fail, and his army falls back to Seminary Ridge and marches away on the night of 4 July
losses: 22,822 by the Stone Sentinels tables: 3,146 killed, 14,510 wounded, 5,166 missing, 24 percent; 23,049 by Busey and Martin. Reynolds, Weed, Vincent, Zook and Farnsworth killed, and Willard, Cross and Sherrill, colonels commanding brigades; Hancock, Gibbon, Sickles, Barlow, Graham, Paul and Stannard among the wounded.

22,709 by the Stone Sentinels tables, which the page calls underreported: 4,400 killed, 12,953 wounded, 5,356 missing, 33 percent; 28,063 by Busey and Martin. Armistead, Garnett, Barksdale, Semmes, Pender, Pettigrew and Avery killed or mortally wounded; Hood, Kemper, Trimble, Heth, Scales, J. M. Jones and G. T. Anderson among the wounded; Archer captured.
outcome.note: About 93,900 Union and 71,700 Confederate troops were engaged by the American Battlefield Trust's count. The Iron Brigade lost 1,150 of 1,830, Iverson's brigade 900 of 1,385, Garnett's 950 of 1,460 and Armistead's 1,230 of 1,950; the 1st Minnesota 215 of 262.

sources: The War Department tablets of 1895 to 1912 and the brigade monuments, as transcribed at gettysburg.stonesentinels.com, with its two strength and casualty tables: every unit's arrival, attack and withdrawal times, its regiments, strengths and losses, and the tablets' positions.

Frederick Tilberg, Gettysburg National Military Park, National Park Service Historical Handbook 9 (1954, rev. 1962): the first shots at Marsh Creek, the opening on Herr Ridge, Reynolds's death, the salient on the 2nd and Culp's Hill on the 3rd.

American Battlefield Trust, 'Gettysburg', for the armies' strengths and losses after Busey and Martin. Emerging Civil War, 'The thunder seemed tame' (2023), for Michael Jacobs's weather observations at Pennsylvania College.

Wikipedia, 'Battle of Gettysburg', its first-day, second-day, Pickett's Charge, Little Round Top, Culp's Hill and third-day cavalry articles and the two orders of battle (read 6 November 2026), for the times and losses the tablets do not give. Busey and Martin's Regimental Strengths and Losses, Pfanz, Coddington, Sears and the Official Records were not consulted directly, nor Bachelder's and Warren's maps.

Terrain: USGS 3DEP elevation at 10 m, sampled to 25 m, with a modern quarry on the Baltimore Pike and Lake Heritage, a 1970s reservoir, filled. Farms, buildings, hills, the roads, the streams and the woods from OpenStreetMap (ODbL); the park avenues, the National Cemetery and the later railways are not drawn. Sunrise and sunset from the NOAA solar formulae, local mean time.

What is reconstructed: positions between the tablets' times are inferred, as are the routes of Longstreet's countermarch, Pickett's approach on the 3rd, Humphreys's night march and Custer's road to the Hanover Road, and the town's streets inside the 1863 town. Brigade losses are spread across each day's fights; where the note gives no figure for a brigade, the loss is an estimate. Long Lane, the Bliss farm and Brinkerhoff's Ridge are placed from the tablets' words. The woods are the park's present outlines, not Warren's survey of 1868. Barksdale's advance is drawn at 5:30, between his tablet's five and Birney's half past six. Stuart's cavalry and the fight on East Cavalry Field are off the map.
